units.text: Etravirine concentrations in seminal plasma in HIV-infected patients

Ten HIV-1 adult antiretroviral-experienced patients receiving an etravirine-containing regimen for at least 1 month were enrolled. Semen and blood samples were both collected around 12Á24 h after the last etravirine dose, depending on once-daily or twice-daily dosing, respectively. HPLC/MS/MS was used to determine etravirine concentrations, and HIV-1 VL was determined by real-time PCR (limit of detection, VL 40 copies/mL).

Ten HIV-1 adult antiretroviral-experienced patients receiving an etravirine-containing regimen for at least 1 month were enrolled. Semen and blood samples were both collected around 12Á24 h after the last etravirine dose, depending on once-daily or twice-daily dosing, respectively. HPLC/MS/MS was used to determine etravirine concentrations, and HIV-1 VL was determined by real-time PCR (limit of detection, VL 40 copies/mL).

Ten blood and twenty semen samples were collected. Median (range) CD4 count was 502 cells/mm 3 (252Á817) and median (range) BP VL was B40 copies/mL (40Á362). Median (range) time on etravirine was 52 weeks (12Á124). Median (range) BP etravirine concentration was 452.5 ng/mL (258Á751). Median (range) SP etravirine concentration was 62.9 ng/mL (31.2Á166), and values were above the protein-free IC 50 range (0.39Á2.4 ng/mL) in all cases. Median (range) etravirine SP:BP ratio was 0.16 (0.07Á0.26). SP VL was B40 copies/mL in all patients, whereas BP VL was detectable in one patient with poor adherence to treatment.

Total etravirine concentrations in male genital secretion are modest, reaching only 16% of the BP concentration, but nevertheless, more than 10 times above the wild type IC 50 range.
